configurations.//: Added Phase 38d-i. Same purpose as refdata-vs-docker (dev server against the dockerized stack) but on 7107, because docker-compose then published every port from 7100 to 7106 and held them whenever the stack is up, colliding with the 7103 that refdata-vs-docker's own vite.docker.config.js pins with strictPort. 7103 was freed when the nats-ui/nui/nats-tower review containers were removed, so refdata-vs-docker works again and this entry is now a spare. The base vite.config already proxies /api/auth to accounts-service (7202) and /api to refdata-service (7201), both host ports of the running stack, so no config override is needed here.
configurations.name: refdata-dev-docker-7107

configurations.//: Added Phase 50e. Same collision refdata-dev-docker-7107 documents: docker-compose publishes the built admin image on 7100, so `admin` (autoPort) lets vite bind localhost:7100 alongside it and every request to 127.0.0.1:7100 still reaches the container, not the dev server. --strictPort on a port docker does not hold is the only way to be sure which one you are looking at.
configurations.name: admin-dev-7108

configurations.//: Use admin-dev-7108 above when the docker stack is up. This entry's autoPort resolves the bind collision on 7100 but not the ambiguity it creates: docker-compose publishes the built admin image there, so requests to 127.0.0.1:7100 keep reaching the CONTAINER while vite serves your edits somewhere else. It is only safe with the stack down.
configurations.name: admin

configurations.//: The shell is containerised (lab-shell/Dockerfile) and published on 7110 by the compose stack; this entry runs the same app from source on the SAME port, so a registry entry curated for the stack stays correct either way and only one of the two can be up at a time. 7100-7106 are held by docker-compose whenever the stack is up and 7107/7108 are claimed above. No autoPort — the shell must be at a known port, since the example plugin (7111) is loaded by URL.
configurations.name: lab-shell

configurations.//: Phase 1b's example plugin. Its own toolchain, its own build, its own server — the shell never compiles it, which is what makes BR-AS03's no-host-rebuild claim testable rather than asserted (lab-shell/tools/hostBundleFingerprint.mjs). strictPort, because the shell reaches it by URL from the curated registry (demos/01-dictionary/registry.json) and a plugin that quietly moved would look like an unreachable remote rather than a moved one. Containerised too (its own Dockerfile), published on the same 7111 by the compose stack.
configurations.name: example-plugin

configurations.//: Contribution preview harness (shared/mfe-preview). Every plugin dev server answers /__preview with its contributions rendered outside the shell. These two entries exist because the compose stack publishes the plugins' own ports (7110-7115) whenever it is up, and each plugin's vite.config pins its port with strictPort — so a CLI --port override on a port docker does not hold is the only way to reach the dev server. 7150+ rather than the next free port, because scripts/new-plugin.sh hands the next sequential port to a NEW plugin and would collide. With the stack down, `example-plugin` / a plain `npm run dev` in the plugin serves /__preview on its normal port instead.
configurations.name: example-plugin-preview-7150

configurations.//: Same 7106 docker-compose collision the other -dev-* entries document. package.json's own dev script hardcodes --port 7106, so this bypasses it with npx vitepress directly. Use when the docs container is up; strictPort so the tab is unambiguously the dev server, not the container.
configurations.name: docs-dev-7109
